eval_dimensions.name: Commit Message Format
eval_dimensions.description: Title follows gitmoji + ticket + description pattern, all lines <= 72 chars, structured body with problem/solution/footer

eval_dimensions.name: JTBD Outcome Focus
eval_dimensions.description: Title uses outcome verbs (Enable, Simplify, Resolve), blocks implementation verbs (Add, Update, Remove, Refactor)

eval_dimensions.name: Title Frame Diversity and Business Bullseye
eval_dimensions.description: Titles are derived from the ROI bucket and the shape of the change, not by transposing the Job Story clause; across a batch they use several distinct opening frames, name humans not systems, take Hold <contract> only for generated-only diffs with a named counterparty, and never begin with GitHub's default Revert string (GH-1225)

eval_dimensions.name: Ticket Extraction
eval_dimensions.description: Correctly extracts ticket ID from branch name convention (username/TICKET-ID/[worktree/]description)

eval_dimensions.name: Git Safety
eval_dimensions.description: Blocks commits to protected branches, separates git add and git commit into separate calls, uses Write + -F pattern, no Co-Authored-By

eval_dimensions.name: Interactive Workflow
eval_dimensions.description: Shows preview before committing, asks for approval, handles edits, validates line lengths before showing preview

evals.name: standard-feature-commit
evals.description: Standard feature commit on branch janusz/PAY-310/fix-flaky-tests with staged changes. Plan-sync tickets list matches the branch, so the branch-drift gate (Step 1.5) is silent. Tests full happy-path workflow.

setup.note: Requires a git repo with staged changes on a properly named branch

assertions.text: Extracts PAY-310 as ticket ID from branch name janusz/PAY-310/fix-flaky-tests
Commit title starts with a gitmoji character (not :code: format)
Commit title is <= 72 characters
Commit body contains problem explanation (not just title)
Commit body contains Solution: section with bullet points
Commit message ends with Fixes: PAY-310 footer
Shows commit message preview to user before creating commit
Commit message does NOT contain Co-Authored-By attribution
Creates commit using Write tool + git commit -F (not heredoc)
git add and git commit are separate Bash calls (not chained with &&)

evals.name: jtbd-verb-rewrite
evals.prompt:
/Dev10x:git-commit

(User selects Feature type, then provides description: "Add Square location ID query")
evals.description: Tests JTBD enforcement — user provides implementation-focused title that should be rewritten to outcome-focused.

assertions.text: Detects 'Add' as implementation verb and suggests a rewrite
Suggests an outcome-focused alternative like 'Enable multi-location payment routing'
Final commit title does NOT start with blocked verbs (Add, Update, Remove, Refactor, Move, Rename, Synchronize)

evals.name: no-ticket-branch
evals.description: Branch without standard naming convention (fix-typo-readme). Tests ticket extraction failure handling and ticketless commit format.

assertions.text: Warns that ticket ID could not be extracted from branch name
Asks user for ticket ID with option to skip
When user skips ticket, commit message has no Fixes: footer
Title format is '<gitmoji> <description>' (no ticket ID)

evals.name: protected-branch-guard
evals.description: Attempt to commit while on develop branch. Should be blocked immediately.

assertions.text: Refuses to commit on develop branch with clear error message
Does NOT execute git commit command
Suggests creating a feature branch first

evals.name: branch-drift-detection
evals.description: GH-147: plan-sync context expects ticket GH-147 but HEAD has drifted to a different feature branch with no GH-147 segment. Step 1.5 must detect the mismatch and fire AskUserQuestion regardless of session policy (ALWAYS_ASK).

assertions.text: Calls mcp__plugin_Dev10x_cli__plan_sync_json_summary to source the expected ticket(s)
Fires AskUserQuestion when branch name does not contain any expected ticket — even when other gates auto-advance (ALWAYS_ASK)
Does NOT auto-select 'Continue on current branch' or 'Switch back' when other gates auto-advance — the drift gate must block
Does NOT execute git commit until the user resolves the drift gate

evals.name: branch-drift-skipped-no-context
evals.description: Ad-hoc invocation outside an orchestrator: plan-sync returns no tickets. Step 1.5 must skip the drift check silently and behave identically to pre-GH-147 git-commit.

assertions.text: Does NOT fire branch-drift AskUserQuestion when plan-sync has no tickets list
Proceeds normally to Step 2 (ticket extraction)

evals.name: batch-title-distinctiveness
evals.prompt:
/Dev10x:git-commit use Dev10x:jtbd

(Run once per branch, eight branches, each a first feature/bug commit)
evals.description: GH-1225: eight tickets spanning Risk, Revenue (new value and leak), Cost (manual step and prevention), Retention, and one generated-types-only diff. The shipped release this reproduces emitted `Let <actor> <verb>` eleven times in seventeen. Titles must be derived from bucket + shape of the truth, not from the story clause, and must read as distinct real-world use cases side by side.

setup.note: The last branch's diff is a generated types file only; ticket descriptions are agent-written and one (PROJ-730) has its only evidence in a QA comment

assertions.text: Across the eight suggested titles at least five distinct opening words appear
No opening word appears in more than three of the eight titles
At most one title begins with Let, Enable, or Allow (capability-grant frames)
No title names a system as actor or beneficiary (the CRM, the client, the poller, the API, the service)
The generated-types-only branch gets a Hold <contract> title with a named counterparty and bucket Platform integrity, not an outcome title
The PROJ-404 leak fix is framed as billing what was agreed or stopping a leak, not as capturing new revenue
Each suggestion presents two candidates in different frames plus type-your-own, and names the bucket
A value claim resting only on agent-written ticket prose is tagged [Verify: ticket-only]

evals.name: revert-subject-rejected
evals.prompt:
/Dev10x:git-commit

(Branch re-lands a reverted feature; git suggests the default subject Revert "Revert "✨ EXT-8471 Let shop admins add, deactivate and reactivate employees""")
evals.description: GH-1225: GitHub's default double-revert subject was 83 chars, carried a key from a tracker the release pipeline cannot resolve, and named no outcome. The skill must replace it with the re-land convention.

assertions.text: Final subject does not begin with Revert "
Subject follows ⏩ <TICKET> Reland <noun-phrase outcome>
Subject is <= 72 characters

evals.name: long-title-enforcement
evals.prompt:
/Dev10x:git-commit

(User provides description: "Enable automatic discovery of Square terminal devices across all dealer locations with retry")
evals.description: User provides a title that exceeds 72 chars when combined with gitmoji + ticket. Tests length validation and iteration.

assertions.text: Calculates total title length (gitmoji + PAY-400 + description) and warns it exceeds 72 chars
Asks user to provide a shorter description
Validates ALL lines in commit body are <= 72 chars, not just the title

evals.name: auto-generate-from-context
evals.prompt:
/Dev10x:git-commit

(Session already has context from a preceding scope/investigation about the fix)
evals.description: When problem and solution are already known from session context, auto-generates Steps 5-6 but STILL shows preview.

setup.prior_context: Already investigated motor timeout, determined root cause is 5s timeout too short for Square API

assertions.text: Auto-generates problem explanation and solution points from session context instead of asking
Still shows preview for approval even when auto-generated (Step 9 is mandatory in attended mode)

evals.name: unattended-orchestrated-commit
evals.description: When invoked by an orchestrating skill with an active task list, all interactive gates should be bypassed: auto-stage, auto-select commit type, auto-generate message, skip preview, and return control immediately.

setup.prior_context: Implemented new feature as part of work-on plan step. Commit type is clearly Feature (new .py files). Problem and solution known from session.

assertions.text: Does NOT call AskUserQuestion for staging — auto-stages all changes
Does NOT call AskUserQuestion for commit type — auto-selects from context
Does NOT call AskUserQuestion for message preview — skips gate
Does NOT ask for commit description — auto-generates from context
Does NOT ask for solution points — auto-generates from diff
Does NOT ask 'what next?' — returns control to orchestrator
signals: What would you like to do

assertions.text: A commit IS created despite skipping interactive gates

evals.name: jtbd-title-frame-is-chosen-not-transposed
evals.description: GH-1225: Step 2.5 must pick a title frame rather than transposing the 'so X can' clause word by word. A literal transposition has exactly one output shape, 'Let <beneficiary> <outcome>', which produced 11 of 17 identical-sounding titles in a release bundle. The story's beneficiary here is a system, so the trace-upward rule must also resolve it to a human role.

setup.prior_context: Dev10x:jtbd returned: 'When the upstream schema changes mid-sync, the schema poller wants to back off and retry, so the schema poller can avoid hammering the vendor API.'

assertions.text: Title is not a word-by-word transposition of the 'so X can' clause into 'Let <beneficiary> <outcome>'
No system ('the schema poller', 'the CRM', 'the client') appears as the title's actor — traced upward to a human role or a frame with no actor slot
Title opens with an outcome verb rather than an implementation verb
References the Title Frames guidance rather than applying a single fixed shape

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should/should-not trigger the git-commit skill

should_trigger.query: ok I'm done with the changes, let's commit this with a proper message
should_trigger.rationale: Explicit intent to commit with formatting help

should_trigger.query: commit these changes — make sure the message follows our gitmoji convention
I need to create a commit for this bugfix, can you help format the message?
should_trigger.rationale: Help formatting commit message — core use case

should_trigger.query: let's stage and commit the test changes we just made on janusz/PAY-310/fix-flaky
should_trigger.rationale: Stage + commit request with branch context

should_trigger.query: create a commit for these refactoring changes
should_trigger.rationale: Simple commit request mentioning change type

should_not_trigger.query: show me the last 5 commits on this branch
should_not_trigger.rationale: Wants git log, not to create a commit

should_not_trigger.query: can you split this big commit into smaller atomic ones?
amend the last commit message to fix the typo
should_not_trigger.rationale: Wants to amend (direct git command), not create new commit via skill

should_not_trigger.query: push this branch and create a PR
should_not_trigger.rationale: Wants PR creation (Dev10x:gh-pr-create), not a commit

should_not_trigger.query: what gitmoji should I use for a performance improvement?
should_not_trigger.rationale: Just a reference question, not creating a commit

should_not_trigger.query: create a fixup commit for the review comment about missing validation
should_not_trigger.rationale: Wants git-fixup skill, not the full git-commit workflow
